title: human-notes.json status-vocabulary + field-schema reconciliation: fix the drift that silently strands analyst-facing notes (sibling of PROP-093; addresses DIRECTIVE-20260613-003)
target: monitor/analyst/human-notes.json: writers (operator/agent-authored HNOTEs emitting status:'active'; decider 'route-to-analyst' HNOTE writer emitting NO status) vs reader (analyst.md Mode 2 dispatcher L223 + Mode 5 filter L312, both require status==='pending'). Cross-file sibling drift confirmed in monitor/decisions/human-notes.json.
problem: DIRECTIVE-20260613-003 reports the EXACT structural sibling of PROP-093 (attention-inbox) in a different file. analyst.md's two reader sites filter live human-notes on status==='pending' only: (1) Mode 2 dispatcher quick-check (L223): const p=n.notes?n.notes.filter(x=>x.status==='pending'):[]; (2) Mode 5 filter (L312): a.filter(n=>n.status==='pending'&&(n.mode===5||/frozen[- ]prediction/...)). Any live note authored with a status OTHER than 'pending' is structurally invisible to the analyst regardless of priority. The dispatcher cleanly reports 'NO NOTES' — a silent strand. This is what happened to HNOTE-OPERATOR-FABLE-MACRO-REVIEW-FOLLOWUPS-001 (authored status:'active', sat 3 days; the operator's priority-bump to 'high' on 2026-06-13 was a no-op because priority is never consulted when status!=='pending'; operator landed an immediate fix flipping it to 'pending'). Investigation confirms TWO divergence axes, not one: (A) STATUS VOCAB — writers emit status:'active' OR omit status entirely, reader matches only 'pending'; (B) FIELD DIVERGENCE — the decider 'route-to-analyst' notes use field 'note' (not the operator-HNOTE convention note_text/body/title) and carry {from,to,iss_ids,type} extras with NO status field at all.

investigation_findings.Q1_writer_sites: Two distinct writer classes emit non-'pending' live notes. (a) status:'active' is emitted by OPERATOR-AUTHORED and AD-HOC AGENT-AUTHORED HNOTEs, not by any templated prompt code path — grep -rn for status active across monitor/prompts/ and monitor/scripts/ returns ZERO write sites. Confirmed authors of the 3 currently-live 'active' notes: operator-cowork sessions (HNOTE-OPERATOR-ISS-2341-2342-REWRITE-COMMISSION-001 in analyst/; HNOTE-OPERATOR-EXP-450-P4-DEFER-001 in decisions/) and a tinker run (HNOTE-TINKER-ISS-2725-PROP093-AUTHORED-001 in decisions/, authored during the PROP-093 run). So 'active' is a HUMAN/AD-HOC convention divergence, not a code path — same hard-to-pin-down shape as PROP-093 C2's undocumented decider write site. (b) MISSING-status is emitted by the decider 'route-to-analyst' HNOTE writer: the 2 live notes HNOTE-DECIDER-1781144487227 / -228 (2026-06-11T02:21Z) have schema {id,created_at,from:'decider',to:'analyst',iss_ids,type:'route-to-analyst',note} with NO status field. This IS a templated decider write path (distinct from the L334 action==='route-to-analyst' block, which writes iss.status + an expansion-tracker entry but does NOT appear to author these human-notes — the exact human-note-emitting site needs locating, analogous to PROP-093 C2's hunt).
investigation_findings.Q2_reader_vs_writer: Recommend BOTH (mirroring PROP-093 C1's choice): widen the reader as a back-compat shim AND normalize writers, with the back-compat clause dropped after >=7 days of clean writes. But ship-conservative per the directive's constraint: Phase 1 = C1 (reader-harden) + C3 (backfill plan); C2 (writer-normalize) is a follow-up because the decider human-note write site is hard to locate (same difficulty PROP-093 C2 hit and which is still pending there).
investigation_findings.Q3_missing_status_notes: NOT legitimately old format — they carry LIVE, never-actioned work. HNOTE-DECIDER-...227 = ISS-2698 (podaac.jpl.nasa.gov timing out HTTP 000 for 3rd consecutive integrity run; needs a verified replacement URL for the PODAAC dataset link + sections.json patch). HNOTE-DECIDER-...228 = ISS-2699 (audit-exp-tracker-gaps.js reports orphan_file=68 > 5-file tolerance; needs orphan triage + tracker update). Both are substantive route-to-analyst work silently stranded since 2026-06-11. Backfill recommendation: set status:'pending' to re-surface (substantive work WAS meant to happen). Operator review is appropriate before bulk-flipping, but the default should be re-surface, not retire.
investigation_findings.Q4_cross_file_drift: CONFIRMED in monitor/decisions/human-notes.json: 2 of 5 notes are status:'active' (HNOTE-OPERATOR-EXP-450-P4-DEFER-001, HNOTE-TINKER-ISS-2725-PROP093-AUTHORED-001). The decider's decisions/human-notes reader is action-typed (it scans for action:'approve_burndown_batch' / 'set_curmudgeon_mode' / 'cancel_burndown' and 'unconsumed' notes per decider.md L155/L852), so plain informational 'active' notes without an action field are read differently than analyst's strict status==='pending' filter — the decisions/ harm is lower but the vocabulary is still divergent. curmudgeon.md (Step 0c, L224) and social.md (L50) BOTH use a strict status:'pending' reader and would strand 'active'/missing-status notes identically; both files are currently EMPTY (0 notes) so no live strand, but the latent defect is the same. Recommendation: generalize the canonical-vocabulary note across all four human-notes readers, but only analyst/ has live stranded items needing action now.
investigation_findings.Q5_consumed_pending_verification: consumed-pending-verification is a NON-TERMINAL state (analyst-mode1-expansions.md L25-47: kept in the LIVE file precisely because the workspace-sync verifier flips it to 'consumed' once verification_artifact_path is observed on disk). CRITICAL: it is NOT a re-work signal for the analyst — the note has ALREADY been actioned and is awaiting an AUTOMATED verifier flip. Therefore C1's widened filter MUST EXCLUDE consumed-pending-verification (and consumed). Widening to include it would re-surface a worked note and could cause the analyst to redo delivered work or race the verifier. The legitimate LIVE-WORK set is {pending, active, missing-status}; the resolution/transitional-but-worked set is {consumed, consumed-pending-verification} and stays invisible to the work dispatcher by design.

proposed_fix.summary: Reconcile to a canonical live-status vocabulary {pending} with a back-compat reader-widen accepting {pending, active, missing-status} during transition; EXCLUDE the resolution states {consumed, consumed-pending-verification}; add a note-text field shim; normalize writers; backfill the 2 stranded route-to-analyst items; document the canonical vocabulary across all four human-notes readers.

changes.change: Mode 2 dispatcher quick-check (L223) and Mode 5 filter (L312): replace the strict x.status==='pending' test with a LIVE-status helper. Define const isLive=s=>(s==='pending'||s==='active'||s===undefined||s===null). Mode 2 dispatcher: n.notes.filter(x=>isLive(x.status)). Add a field shim so the note text resolves across schema variants: treat (x.note_text||x.note||x.body||x.title) as the note text wherever Mode 2's downstream procedure reads the note. Mode 5: widen to (n.status==='pending'||n.status==='active') ONLY — do NOT include missing-status in Mode 5 (Mode 5 must never self-trigger; its mode===5||/frozen[- ]prediction/ guard already gates it, and the missing-status route-to-analyst notes do not match that guard, so they won't trigger Mode 5 anyway). CRITICAL (Q5): the widened set MUST NOT include consumed or consumed-pending-verification — the latter is a non-terminal-but-already-worked state awaiting the workspace-sync verifier flip; re-surfacing it would cause redo/race. Add an inline comment at both sites documenting the canonical vocabulary: live={pending(canonical), active(back-compat), missing(back-compat)}; resolution/transitional-worked={consumed, consumed-pending-verification} stay invisible to the work dispatcher.
changes.rationale: Makes the 2 stranded route-to-analyst items and any future active/missing-status note reachable, without re-surfacing already-worked resolution states. The pending||active||missing clause is the back-compat transition window; once C2 lands and writers emit pending, a later Mode 3 cleanup drops the active/missing tolerance.

changes.change: TWO writer classes. (a) DECIDER route-to-analyst human-note writer: locate the exact decider code path that authors {from:'decider',to:'analyst',type:'route-to-analyst',note} HNOTEs into monitor/analyst/human-notes.json (the 227/228 notes; NOTE this is distinct from the L334 action-branch which writes iss.status + expansion-tracker, and the human-note-emitting site is not obviously that block — it needs locating, OPEN QUESTION mirroring PROP-093 C2). Once located, add status:'pending' to the emitted object and standardize the text field to note_text (or keep note and rely on C1's shim). (b) OPERATOR/AGENT HNOTE-authoring convention: standardize on status:'pending' for new live notes; document in the relevant prompts (tinker's own HNOTE-authoring step, since tinker authored an 'active' note this lineage) and in CLAUDE.md 'Human Notes Rule' that the canonical live status is pending, not active. 'active' is deprecated back-compat.
changes.rationale: Single durable source so the ||active||missing back-compat clause can eventually be dropped. Class (a) is the templated path that produced the live strand; class (b) is the human/ad-hoc convention. Class (a) is the higher-value fix (it recurs automatically).

Once C1 lands, the next analyst Mode 2 run picks them up automatically even without the backfill (isLive treats missing-status as live), so the backfill is belt-and-suspenders; C1 alone unblocks them. (2) analyst/ HNOTE-OPERATOR-ISS-2341-2342-REWRITE-COMMISSION-001 (active): operator decides pending (re-surface) vs consumed (retire) — its body says operator-blocked pending EXP-452 P1/P8, so it may be a legitimate hold; default to leaving it active until operator confirms (C1 will make it visible regardless, which is correct if it's truly live). (3) decisions/ 2 'active' notes: operator confirms intent — EXP-450-P4-DEFER reads as a deliberate defer marker (likely keep as-is or convert to a dedicated defer/consumed state); TINKER-ISS-2725 is an informational ask the decider's action-typed reader handles separately. Do NOT mass-flip the consumed / consumed-pending-verification notes (constraint).
changes.rationale: The directive's no-mass-flip constraint: only the live-state-confused items (active + missing-status) are in scope; resolution states are intentional and stay.

changes.change: curmudgeon and social readers use the same strict status:'pending' filter and would strand active/missing-status notes; both files are currently EMPTY so no live action is needed, but apply the same canonical-vocabulary documentation note and (optionally) the same isLive widen for symmetry to prevent future drift. decider's decisions/human-notes reader is action-typed (reads action: fields + 'unconsumed'); recommend it ALSO recognize the canonical live vocabulary so plain informational 'active'/missing-status notes aren't ambiguous. This is a doc + defensive-widen generalization, lower priority than C1 (analyst is the only file with live stranded items).
changes.rationale: Prevents the same drift recurring in the other three human-notes pairs. Confirmed latent in curmudgeon/social readers; confirmed live (2 active notes) in decisions/.

proposed_fix.decision_A_vs_B: BOTH reader-widen (C1) AND writer-normalize (C2), exactly as PROP-093 C1 chose. C1 is required regardless (it's the unblock and the back-compat safety net); C2 makes pending durable so the back-compat clause can later drop. The directive's Q2 explicitly recommends BOTH unless evidence argues otherwise — no contrary evidence found.

C2(a) needs it located — same hunt PROP-093 C2 is still blocked on. grep for 'route-to-analyst' + 'human-notes' co-occurrence and any decider helper that dual-writes notes.

For the 2 decisions/ 'active' notes: is EXP-450-P4-DEFER-001 a deliberate long-lived defer marker (keep active / give it a dedicated 'deferred' status) or should it normalize to pending? Operator intent needed.

Should CLAUDE.md 'Human Notes Rule' be amended to state the canonical live status is pending (with active deprecated)? Recommend yes — it stops the human-authoring convention from re-introducing 'active'.

Should C4's defensive isLive widen be applied to curmudgeon.md/social.md now (symmetry, zero live items) or deferred until those files actually see drift? Recommend apply-now for symmetry since it's cheap and the readers are identical.
test_plan: T1 reader-visibility-active: fixture analyst human-notes with 1 status:'active' note -> Mode 2 dispatcher counts it (was 0 before C1).
T2 reader-visibility-missing: fixture with 1 missing-status route-to-analyst note (note field, no status) -> Mode 2 dispatcher counts it AND the field shim resolves the text via x.note.
T3 resolution-state-excluded: fixture with 1 consumed-pending-verification note -> Mode 2 dispatcher counts 0 (must NOT re-surface; Q5 guard).
T4 consumed-excluded: fixture with 1 consumed note -> Mode 2 counts 0.
T5 mode5-no-self-trigger: fixture missing-status route-to-analyst note (not mode 5, no frozen-pred text) -> Mode 5 filter yields 0 (widen did not over-trigger Mode 5).
T6 writer-normalize (after C2): trigger the decider route-to-analyst human-note path in a scratch run -> emitted note has status:'pending'.
T7 no-regression: existing canonical pending notes processed identically.
T8 cross-file (C4): curmudgeon/social readers count a fixture active note after the defensive widen; no change to behavior when files empty.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land C1 (analyst.md reader harden + field shim + Q5 exclusion) FIRST — it is the unblock, makes the 2 stranded route-to-analyst items reachable on the next analyst Mode 2 run, and is safe (additive filter widen, excludes resolution states, back-compat).
Phase 2: C3 backfill (operator review of the 'active' notes' intent) — largely redundant once C1 lands for the missing-status items, needed only for the operator-judgment items.
Phase 3: land C2 (writer normalize) once the divergent decider human-note write site is located; amend CLAUDE.md Human Notes Rule canonical vocabulary.
Phase 4: C4 cross-file generalize (curmudgeon/social/decider readers + docs).
Phase 5: after >=7 days with all writers on status:'pending' and 0 active/missing-status live notes observed, drop the ||active||missing back-compat clause from C1 (tinker Mode 3 verification).
tradeoffs: Gain: closes a recurring silent-strand class (the SECOND confirmed instance of this exact status-vocabulary defect family after PROP-093's attention-inbox; the human-notes variant has HIGHER live harm because 2 genuine site-fix work items, ISS-2698 broken PODAAC link + ISS-2699 orphan audit, are actively stranded). Cost / the-other-side: (1) C2's decider write-site hunt may be as hard as PROP-093 C2's (still pending) — if it can't be cleanly located, C1 alone (reader harden with back-compat kept permanently) still closes the visibility gap, just less tidily. (2) Widening the reader risks re-surfacing notes that were intentionally parked at 'active' (e.g., EXP-450-P4-DEFER as a defer marker) — mitigated by routing those to operator judgment in C3 and by the fact that a visible 'parked' note is a smaller harm than a silently-lost work item. (3) An observer could argue the decisions/curmudgeon/social variants are out-of-scope churn (directive's not_in_scope says 'beyond noting whether drift exists') — C4 is therefore scoped as doc + optional defensive widen, not mandatory. (4) The Q5 exclusion is load-bearing: getting it wrong (including consumed-pending-verification in the live filter) would cause the analyst to redo verified work or race the verifier — the test plan T3 guards this explicitly. Conservative path: ship C1 immediately (it's safe and it's the unblock); treat C2/C3/C4 as reviewed follow-ups. Residual risk low: all changes are prompt-logic/doc edits, none touch wins.json or sections.json.
estimated_impact: Unblocks 2 silently-stranded route-to-analyst work items (ISS-2698 broken PODAAC dataset link — a live site defect; ISS-2699 orphan_file=68 audit) plus 1 operator-judgment 'active' note in analyst/human-notes.json; prevents forward silent-strand of any future active/missing-status human note across all four human-notes files; documents one canonical live-status vocabulary. No compute/disk impact — prompt + doc edits only.
why_human_needed: Three judgment calls: (1) locating + normalizing the divergent decider route-to-analyst human-note write site (C2a) — the templated source, hard to pin like PROP-093 C2; (2) intent of the 2 decisions/ 'active' notes and the analyst/ 'active' operator-blocked note (C3) — keep/defer/retire is operator-domain; (3) whether to amend CLAUDE.md Human Notes Rule + apply C4 defensive widen now vs later. C1 (analyst reader harden) is safe enough to apply without those answers and should ship first.
